title: Grudges were held.
transcript: This is the final thing I'm gonna say about CAN Lions. At the Dark Room Villa panel, when I said, creators have the most power in the room right now, it was really, really personal to me, because 18 months ago, a big ad publication that I will not name wrote a nasty piece of shitty journalism where my name in work was the punchline, which was, you can't learn advertising on TikTok. I felt so much shame that I didn't create content for weeks after that. So to be at CAN this year, where creators were celebrated, where the gatekeepers held the door open and our work was validated, felt so good. I have worked in the advertising industry for 10 years, I've made content for advertisers for six. And at this point, we all know the big kind of cliche takeaway from CAN this year is, hey, creators are really important to the future of advertising. And for those of us who create and consume online, we've known that for years. But for the industry giants, for the slow moving institution that actually steers this business, it is new, it is novel, and it's been and worth repeating for them. For me, what's really exciting about it is that for a time right now, the power is truly in the hands of individuals from all backgrounds. For those of us who have a unique POV and decide to hit publish. So a huge thanks to the darkroom villa For being a massive safe haven for my introvert soul this week. Thanks to Orange John, Josh, Levine, and Matt from Whisper Flow for sharing your genius with me on the panel. And thank you so much to you who watched to the end, because, yeah, I wrote the script a little drunk on the plane home. Love you. Bye.
